findings.title: Classifying only the first shell token misgrades review evidence
findings.trigger: A report records a wrapped no-op such as `env true`, or a compound inspection command beginning with `echo`.
findings.execution_path: assess_report filters commands with integer exit codes, calls _first_program, and compares only that first program against TRIVIAL_COMMANDS. Its status is consumed by the review runner and acceptance readiness.
findings.consequence: The new hollow-report guard accepts no-op-only evidence as complete, while legitimate compound inspection commands can incorrectly make a review incomplete.
findings.evidence: An otherwise valid report returned incomplete for `true`, complete for both `env true` and `command true`, and incomplete for `echo inspecting; git diff HEAD~1..HEAD`. Added tests cover simple commands and environment assignments, but neither wrappers nor compound shell commands.
findings.suggested_fix: Account for common execution wrappers and compound shell commands, or require structured per-command evidence. Add regression cases for both wrapped no-ops and compound commands containing actual inspection.
